summary: Measured interpretation of the leader-side loop experiment, now asserted. Receipt CheckRun 7772ad1b5b154d498a27a79806bb0ea7 (exit 0, completed), parsed indices: 3 = loop_observe defect sub-case (stale_index_entry=true, snapshot_index=8, install_snapshot_calls_early=2778, install_snapshot_calls_late=16207, follower_applied_index=8 pinned, follower_last_index=8, leader_last_index=9, leader_commit_index=9), 1 = loop_observe control sub-case (install_snapshot_calls_early=1, late=1, follower_applied_index=9, follower_last_index=9), 0 and 2 = both sub-cases reaching the same leader snapshot at index 8. Conclusion violated / defect_claim asserted: a follower holding an earlier-term entry at the leader's snapshot index L is unrepairable — the follower rejects PrevLogEntry=L, the leader rewinds nextIndex to L, setPreviousLog(L) needs the compacted-away entry L-1 so replicateTo branches to SEND_SNAP, sendLatestSnapshot restores nextIndex=L+1, and the identical rejection recurs; over the 1.2 s window the peer received ~13.4k more snapshots while its applied index never moved off L. The control peer, differing only by the absence of that earlier-term entry, converged after exactly one snapshot, which excludes single-voter leadership, AddVoter and compaction as competing causes. Recorded counterevidence (the leader's own commit index still reached 9, so the non-progress is scoped to that follower's replication) and limitations (InmemStore only, seeded precondition, TrailingLogs=0, in-process transport), leaving the multi-node-history reachability gap open. Also added a Fact knowledge entry with the observed operands and the frozen-snapshot conditions. Structural validation returned valid=true.
